newsitem.title: USA: General Instrument holders okay restructuring.
newsitem.headline: General Instrument holders okay restructuring.

text.p: General Instrument Corp said Wednesday its shareholders approved its restructuring plan, splitting it into three separate new public companies.
Shares of each of the new companies will likely begin trading on a "when issued" basis on the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday, July 24. Regular trading is expected to start on Monday, July 28.

The three new companies are NextLevel Systems Inc, a supplier of systems and components for communications networks, CommScope Inc, a manufacturer of coaxial cables and high-performance electronic cables, and General Semiconductor Inc, a provider of power rectifiers and voltage suppressors.
For each outstanding share of General Instrument stock, holders will receive one share of NextLevel, one-third share of CommScope and one-quarter share of General Semiconductor.
There will be about 149 million NextLevel shares outstanding, 49 million CommScope and 37 million General Semiconductor.
General Istrument said NextLevel is expected to report second quarter financial results on July 28, CommScope on July 29 and General Semiconductor on July 30.
